name: basement-membrane-v1
title: Basement membrane v1 — collagen IV network modulus & remodelling for the AICS vertex model
description:
This investigation is the clean-room Vivarium build of the AICS-Lumenoids
"Basement membrane — v1 model specification" (Roam graph, exported 2026-09-30;
the source spec and diagram are in `workspace/references/`). Every model
parameter is transcribed from the spec's parameter sheet and labelled as such.
The authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public
(github.com/Billie1717/BasementMembraneTurnoverSims, Zenodo
10.5281/zenodo.20719515, commit `ab4c004`); this build remains a transcription
from the spec rather than a port of those scripts, and they are the ground
truth to cross-check its parameters against (not yet done — decision below).

**Engines.** The workspace imports two already-wrapped simulators —
`viva-lammps` (the `LAMMPSProcess` bridge) and `viva-smoldyn` — and builds the
collagen IV network on top of the real LAMMPS engine. LAMMPS runs stages 1–2
(rigid rods, junction flexibility); Smoldyn is held for stage 3 (flexible
fibers + surface binders) per spec decision #2.

**Staged build (spec "v1 build").**
  - Stage 1 — reproduce the paper; separate elastic from viscous. Stretch,
    hold, then switch the crosslink chemistry on. Reports an elastic modulus
    and a stress-relaxation time.  ← this investigation's first study.
  - Stage 2 — growing substrate (flat): impose equibiaxial strain rate ε̇,
    read off σ(ε̇); an effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ and the rate at which the
    response turns elastic.
  - Stage 3 — add the cell–BM linker (surface-attached springs, constant
    off-rate). Smoldyn's surface binders land here.
  - Stage 4 — curvature (only if stages 2–3 depend on R beyond ε̇ = Ṙ/R).

**Coupling route (spec decision).** Offline first: tabulate the BM's modulus
and remodelling time against growth rate and hand them to the vertex model.
Then direct: vertex-mesh surface velocities drive the BM substrate, BM stress
feeds back, exchanged every N vertex steps.

**Visualization (reviewer round 1, 2026-10-07).** Each study's Simularium
trajectory now embeds its diagnostic plots directly (stress-vs-strain, the
stress/strain time series, crosslinks) and draws the periodic simulation box
as a per-frame outline that deforms with the imposed strain. The stretch
movies are made coherent (each bead at its nearest periodic image of the
network centroid), so boundary crossings no longer teleport across timepoints.
See `feedback/` for the imported reviewer file.

at_a_glance.role: Stage 1 + the cross-check headline. Runs the staged protocol with the parameters corrected to the released code. Modulus is very soft, consistent with zero at v1 size (~±1 Pa) and with the published ≈0.03 Pa; the remodelling mechanism is correct but τ is below detection at v1 scale. Carries the cross-check and modulus-ladder figures.

Stage 2 + the coupling deliverable. Sweeps the equibiaxial growth rate ε̇ and, from the faithful density-calibrated model, tabulates the effective modulus E(ε̇) (≈7→11 Pa, stiffening with rate) and remodelling time τ(ε̇) (≈36–51 τ, ≈constant) — the two numbers the AICS vertex model takes (offline coupling).

Follow-up (explanation superseded). The rigidity-percolation story is retired by the cross-check: the released model has junction angles, so it is not a central-force network and z<4 does not explain its softness. The sweep now documents only that our angles-off transcription is sub-isostatic and soft.

Follow-up (reframed). Bending is a released feature (NC1 k=4.0), not an add-on. Swept around k=4.0: our as-formed-restraint realization is ill-conditioned and bending does not make the network stiff — the released model has the angles and is still soft. A faithful run needs angles active during assembly.

Geometric readouts (spec "has: geometrical structure"). Reads porosity + bundling off the real network against measured BM. Pore diameter reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density; the NC1/7S-only topology under-bundles (mean ~1 protomer/strand, below the measured 5–7), because the released model has no lateral-association bond. Carries the evidence map.

glossary.definition: One collagen IV triple-helical molecule (~376 nm end-to-end); modelled as one two-bead rod.
The two crosslinking ends of a protomer. NC1 binds 1 partner (hexamer), 7S binds 3 (tetramer/spider).
The viscous stress-relaxation time set by crosslink make/break kinetics; calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.
Equibiaxial in-plane strain rate. A sphere of radius R growing at Ṙ stretches its shell at ε̇ = Ṙ/R.

question: What effective elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time does a coarse-grained collagen IV basement-membrane network produce on a growing (biaxially stretching) boundary — the two numbers the AICS 3D vertex model needs to couple to a basement membrane?
hypothesis: A standalone collagen IV network, coarse-grained at the fiber scale (one protomer = one two-bead rod, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume), reproduces the Meadowcroft/Barrientos regime: a very soft elastic modulus (the published network's own linear modulus is ≈0.03 Pa) and a crosslink- turnover-limited stress-relaxation time that can be calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime. Its effective modulus and remodelling time, tabulated against growth rate ε̇, become inputs to the vertex model (offline coupling first).

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The staged protocol runs end-to-end on real LAMMPS, a crosslinked network assembles from two-bead rods, the stress-strain ramp yields a finite (very soft) elastic modulus, and the chemistry-on hold shows a measurable stress relaxation, or a noise-limited null at v1 network size.
The ε̇ sweep runs and returns σ(ε̇) and an effective viscosity η per rate, with the viscous and elastic regimes identified at v1 parameters.
The connectivity sweep shows z stays below 4 and the modulus stays consistent with zero, establishing that rigidity requires junction bending / bundling.
Junction bending is implemented and dominates the mechanics (floppy baseline ~0 → large |E|); a reproducible modulus is blocked on network size and a pre-stress-free measurement.

executive.what_is_this: The first Vivarium build of the AICS lumenoid basement membrane: a coarse- grained collagen IV network on a moving boundary, run until it reports an elastic modulus and a remodelling time for the vertex model.
executive.verdict: COMPLETE (2026-10-02). The research question is answered and the coupling deliverable produced. A faithful clean-room model (cross-checked against the released code — structure, parameters, junction angles verified against the bond/react template, density from the authors' own dataNucType9_dense) now reproduces the published modulus, separates a reproducible elastic modulus from a reproducible remodelling time, and tabulates E(ε̇) and τ(ε̇) for the vertex model (bm-v2). Open handoffs, both documented and neither a model gap: the absolute-Pa energy-scale decision (spec #4, AICS's call) and the GCE / distance- gated-break kinetics for the exact equilibrium crosslink fraction. --- The clean-room build was cross-checked against the authors' now-public code (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) and its parameters corrected to match (2026-10-01). Three findings: (1) Cross-check — the model structure and central-force parameters match the released code (two-bead rods, NC1×1/7S×3, no excluded volume, kT=1, dt=0.01, FactorMult=0.66, MP=0.12, rod k=200), but the released model is bending- stabilized (NC1 angle k=4.0 @180°, plus 7S angles @155°/60°) and diverged on crosslink bond stiffness, rod length (now corrected to 3σ → σ≈125 nm), Langevin damp, cutoffs, Nevery, break mechanism and GCE monomer exchange. (2) Corrected re-run — with the released parameters the v1 network is very soft: the elastic modulus is small and consistent with zero at this network size (~±1 Pa across seeds), consistent with the published model's own ≈0.03 Pa linear modulus. The remodelling mechanism is correct but τ is below detection at v1 scale. (3) Retired explanation — the central-force rigidity-percolation story (bm-v3) is retired: the released model has junction angles, so z<4 does not explain its mechanics. (4) Faithful angles (2026-10-02) — creating the released NC1 angles DURING assembly (real harmonic angles via create_bonds single/angle, matching the released bond/react templates) resolves the ill-conditioning: the modulus becomes positive, reproducible across seeds, and well-conditioned (bm-v4). So once the angles are faithfully active the network is NOT floppy — its modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent. (5) Elastic/viscous separation + density calibration — with per-angle deletion the stiff faithful network REMODELS in the viscous hold, and with the geometry set to the authors' dense initial config (3.0 rods/σ², 12σ-thick slab, read from Assembly/input/dataNucType9_dense) the result is well-defined: make+break and make-only AGREE (≈2.6 crosslinks/rod), and the model separates a reproducible elastic modulus (E ≈ 3 LJ ≈ 6 Pa) from a reproducible remodelling time (τ ≈ 40–60 τ) — the study's core goal, where both were noise-limited before. (6) The model reproduces the published modulus — the junction angles were verified to match the released bond/react template exactly (2 per crosslink, 7S-NC1-NC1 at type 1), and at the authors' density the modulus rises with crosslink fraction and PASSES THROUGH the published ≈0.03 Pa near percolation (~0.8 crosslinks/rod), reaching ~8 Pa when saturated. So the published softness is a near-percolation (sparse-crosslink) state, not a model-structure gap, and the apparent "200× discrepancy" dissolves: the faithful model spans the published value. The one open kinetic detail is which equilibrium crosslink fraction the authors' GCE + distance-gated breaking settles at; the ABSOLUTE Pa also still depends on the energy-scale decision (spec #4).
decisions_needed: Absolute (Pa) modulus path: the faithful angle-stabilized model now reproduces the published ≈0.03 Pa and gives a reproducible reduced-unit modulus (bm-v4, E≈3 LJ). An EXACT absolute value additionally needs the released GCE + distance-gated 7S break (0.95) + dense initial config — implement these, or accept the reduced-unit value and resolve via the energy-scale decision (#4)? (Cross-check + param correction already DONE 2026-10-01; see references/cross-check-vs-released-code.md.)
Engine for stages 1–2: LAMMPS now; revisit Smoldyn at stage 3 (spec #2).
Secretion: fixed concentration vs fixed flux (spec #3).
Energy scale: report modulus in Pa (fit to a measured modulus) or keep kT and report a ratio (spec #4).
Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the BM — basal tension, mobility, or elastic spring (spec #5).
Linker values: density, spring constant, off-rate; sweep off-rate as a multiple of the crosslink break rate (spec #6).
Growth rate ε̇ from the lumenoid radius time course — still requested (spec #7).
Slab thickness / layer count — one z-stack away (spec #9).
Which readout calibrates vs validates — remodelling time calibrates MP and the time unit, so it cannot also validate (spec #10).
